title: Successive lower truncations have a two-term kernel quasi-isomorphic to one cohomology object
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and let $K$ be a cochain complex with cohomology objects $H^r(K)=\ker(d^r)/\operatorname{im}(d^{r-1})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an integer $m$, write $\tau_{\ge m}K$ for the canonical lower truncation: it is zero in degrees below $m$, is $K^m/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})$ in degree $m$, and is $K^r$ in degrees $r>m$, with the induced differentials. The canonical transition is the quotient map $q_m:\tau_{\ge m}K\to\tau_{\ge m+1}K$. Define the two-term complex $C_m(K)$ to be $K^m/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})$ in degree $m$, $\operatorname{im}(d^m)$ in degree $m+1$, zero elsewhere, with differential induced by $d^m$. Then there is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes
$$0\to C_m(K)\to\tau_{\ge m}K\xrightarrow{q_m}\tau_{\ge m+1}K\to0,$$
where the inclusion is the identity in degree $m$, the inclusion $\operatorname{im}(d^m)\hookrightarrow K^{m+1}$ in degree $m+1$, and zero elsewhere. There is a natural morphism of complexes $H^m(K)[-m]\to C_m(K)$ which is the canonical inclusion $\ker(d^m)/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})\hookrightarrow K^m/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})$ in degree $m$ and zero elsewhere; it is a quasi-isomorphism. All these constructions are natural in morphisms of complexes.

proof.text: At degree $m$ the map $C_m(K)\to\tau_{\ge m}K$ is the identity of $K^m/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})$, and at degree $m+1$ it is the inclusion $\operatorname{im}(d^m)\hookrightarrow K^{m+1}$; it is zero in all other degrees. By the definition of the lower truncation in the statement, $q_m$ is zero in degree $m$ (where $\tau_{\ge m+1}K$ is zero), the quotient $K^{m+1}\to K^{m+1}/\operatorname{im}(d^m)$ in degree $m+1$, and the identity of $K^r$ in degrees $r>m+1$. Thus the displayed sequence is exact in every degree: in degree $m$ it is $0\to K^m/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}K^m/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})\to0\to0$, in degrees $r>m+1$ it is $0\to0\to K^r\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}K^r\to0$, in degrees below $m$ all terms are zero, and in degree $m+1$ the kernel of the quotient $K^{m+1}\to K^{m+1}/\operatorname{im}(d^m)$ is $\operatorname{im}(d^m)$. The maps commute with the differentials: in degree $m$ because the differential of $C_m(K)$ is induced by $d^m$, and in degree $m+1$ because $d^{m+1}d^m=0$, so $d^{m+1}$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}(d^m)$. Hence it is a short exact sequence of complexes. This is the lower-truncation construction of Stacks Tag 0118.

proof.text: The degree-$m$ component of $H^m(K)[-m]\to C_m(K)$ is the canonical inclusion $\ker(d^m)/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})\hookrightarrow K^m/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})$, and the other components are zero. This is a morphism of complexes because the source has zero differential and the differential of $C_m(K)$, induced by $d^m$, vanishes on $\ker(d^m)$. The cohomology of $C_m(K)$ in degree $m$ is the kernel of the map $K^m/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})\to\operatorname{im}(d^m)$ induced by $d^m$, namely $\ker(d^m)/\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})=H^m(K)$, and the map above induces the identity on it; its cohomology in degree $m+1$ is $\operatorname{im}(d^m)/\operatorname{im}(d^m)=0$ since that map is an epimorphism; all other cohomology objects vanish, as do those of $H^m(K)[-m]$ outside degree $m$. Therefore the map is a quasi-isomorphism by the definition of quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0118 (homology-section-truncations), identification of the successive quotient with H^m(K)[-m]

proof.text: For a morphism of complexes $f:K\to L$, $f$ maps $\operatorname{im}(d_K^{r})$ into $\operatorname{im}(d_L^{r})$ and $\ker(d_K^r)$ into $\ker(d_L^r)$ and induces the corresponding maps on quotients and images. The maps $f^m$ and $f^{m+1}$ therefore define a morphism $C_m(K)\to C_m(L)$, and $f$ induces morphisms $\tau_{\ge m}K\to\tau_{\ge m}L$ and $\tau_{\ge m+1}K\to\tau_{\ge m+1}L$ forming a morphism between the two short exact sequences. The inclusion $H^m(K)[-m]\to C_m(K)$ commutes with these induced maps because it is the canonical map from cycles modulo boundaries and $H^m(f)$ is induced by $f^m$. Thus the short exact sequences and the quasi-isomorphisms are natural in $K$.
